Prepare the Standard upgrade packet (verified info + demo video showing the OAuth flow)

approval.cost: No fee for app registration, Trial, or Standard access is stated anywhere in the docs read
approval.trigger: Two human reviews gate this API. (1) Trial access review, required before you get credentials at all: you submit the Connect app request form; 'Application requests are reviewed by Pinterest. You will receive an email notification after your app has been reviewed, letting you know whether it was approved or denied access.' Documented denial reasons: 'Privacy policy is inaccurate or not accessible' (it must load completely, be publicly accessible, and be hosted on a domain clearly associated with your company/app) and 'App description is incomplete or unclear'. Caps under Trial: everything you create is sandboxed: 'all Pins and Boards created with Trial access are only visible to their creator as Sandbox entities' (reads of boards, Pins, analytics, ads, and catalogs work in both tiers); rate limits are 'calls per day/per app' with daily limits varying by category; no numeric user/install cap for Trial is stated. (2) Standard access upgrade review, required before offering the integration to real users or creating publicly visible content: prerequisites are Trial approval, compliance with the Developer Guidelines, plus 'a video recording of your app completing an action using the Pinterest API. We will review to verify that you are sending users through the OAuth flow appropriately and not storing any sensitive information.' Steps: My apps > Upgrade on the app card > verify previously submitted info (use case, privacy policy link) > upload the video demo > submit. Denial reasons include: demo video doesn't show the authentication flow; demo uses a non-approved auth method ('such as collecting user login credentials or Pinterest session cookies'); demo doesn't show a live Pinterest integration (wireframes/general demos may be denied). Standard access lifts the sandbox visibility and switches rate limits to 'calls per minute/per user/per app'. No app directory/marketplace listing process is documented; distribution is direct via your own product.
approval.wait: 'Standard upgrade requests are reviewed regularly. You will receive an email notification once a decision has been made on your app.' And: 'Please allow a few days for teams to review your access requests before following up on your app's overall status.' No fixed SLA is published

blockers.detail: API writes succeed but Pins/Boards are invisible to everyone except their creator until you pass Standard review. Nothing errors; the content simply isn't public.
blockers.howToClear: Do not interpret successful Trial writes as production readiness; pass Standard before real users create content.
blockers.title: The Trial sandbox trap

blockers.detail: You cannot get credentials without passing Trial review, and you cannot serve real users meaningfully without passing Standard review with a video demo that must show the OAuth flow and a live integration.
blockers.howToClear: Record the demo as a launch deliverable: real OAuth flow, real API action, no credential collection.
blockers.title: Two-stage approval before production

blockers.detail: Apps created on or after September 25, 2025 automatically use continuous refresh tokens (60-day expiration, refreshable indefinitely), while older apps silently keep the legacy behavior (refresh_token_expires_in 31536000, 365 days, in the code-exchange example) unless they pass continuous_refresh=true at code exchange. A lapsed continuous refresh token (more than 60 days without refreshing) means the user must re-authorize.
blockers.howToClear: Refresh well inside the 60-day window, and opt older apps into continuous refresh at exchange.
blockers.title: The September 25, 2025 refresh-token regime change

alternatives: Client Credentials grant (the app acts on its own behalf, machine-to-machine; tokens carry a pinc prefix vs pina for user tokens; caveat: 'you cannot use certain endpoints that provide read/write access to more sensitive data'; each endpoint's reference page lists whether Client Credentials is accepted)
Product limited tokens / test tokens (once an app is approved for Trial, generate a token to test the API without building the OAuth flow; 'Test tokens expire after 24 hours')
flavor.recommended: The Authorization Code grant on a Pinterest app, upgraded from Trial to Standard access
flavor.why: The object is an app registered in the Pinterest developer portal under My apps, yielding an App ID (the OAuth client_id) and an app secret. Access is tiered per app: every approved app starts on Trial access and can be upgraded to Standard access. Pinterest's docs say the Authorization Code grant 'is designed for web apps that access a user's data on behalf of that user. It is the only grant type that gives you access to the full range of capabilities offered by the Pinterest API', and 'Use this grant type if you are building an app to be used by multiple, independent end users, or customers.' Scopes use {entity}:read / {entity}:write syntax (ads, billing, biz_access, boards, catalogs, pins, user_accounts; secret content needs special variants such as boards:read_secret). No API-key-only auth exists for user data; everything is OAuth 2.0.

humanMust: Have a Pinterest account and verify your account's email address; accept the Developer Terms of Service in My apps
Click Connect app and submit the request form for Trial access (app name must include at least 3 Latin letters/numbers and can't contain the word 'Pinterest')
Once approved, retrieve the App ID and app secret (My apps > Manage > Configure) and configure redirect URI(s)
When ready for production, request the Standard access upgrade with the demo video
name: Pinterest
nuances: Access tokens live 30 days (expires_in 2592000 in both Authorization Code and Client Credentials examples): 'Refresh your access token before it expires, within 30 days (2592000 seconds) after it is issued.' Refresh calls may include an optional narrower scope to get a down-scoped access token; refresh responses return refresh_token_expires_in 5184000 (60 days) and a refresh_token_expires_at timestamp.

Leaked-token revocation: Pinterest is in GitHub's secret scanning partner program; if a token leaks in a public repo, 'The exposed token's access is revoked within 24 hours', and the user must reconnect. Tokens also go invalid if the user changes their username or password, and 'Pinterest does not always notify you if that has happened.' Expired/invalid tokens return HTTP 401 with API error code 2.

Resetting the app secret (My apps > Configure > Reset app secret) keeps existing access tokens working, but no new tokens can be minted with the old secret. Redirect URIs require exact match, and the redirect target 'must not cause the responding server to send a secondary redirect to yet another URI'.

Doc bug worth knowing: in the Client Credentials parameter table, the docs say to set grant_type to authorization_code; the worked example correctly uses grant_type=client_credentials. Follow the example. The token endpoint uses HTTP Basic auth with the App ID as username and client secret as password (credentials in the header, not the body).
prerequisites: A Pinterest account with a verified email address
A publicly accessible privacy policy on a domain clearly associated with your company/app
Redirect URI(s) that exactly match and do not redirect onward

steps.detail: Have a Pinterest account, verify your email address, go to My apps, and accept the Developer Terms of Service. Click Connect app and complete the request form, then submit your request for Trial access; Pinterest reviews it and emails an approve/deny decision.
steps.title: Request Trial access

steps.detail: My apps > Manage > Configure: retrieve the App ID and app secret, and configure redirect URI(s) (multiple accepted; exact match required).
steps.title: Get credentials; configure redirect URIs

steps.detail: Redirect the user to pinterest.com/oauth/ with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope (required, at least one), and optional state. The user logs in and approves the scopes. Verify state on return, then POST api.pinterest.com/v5/oauth/token with HTTP Basic auth (App ID as username, secret as password) and body grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri. Store the access_token + refresh_token server-side. (Apps created before Sept 25, 2025: include continuous_refresh=true in this exchange for a continuous refresh token.)
steps.title: Run the authorization code flow

steps.detail: Call the API with Authorization: Bearer. Refresh before the 30-day access-token expiry and before the 60-day continuous refresh token lapses ('Repeat these steps before 60 days in order to keep the continuous refresh token valid').
steps.title: Call the API; refresh on the 30/60-day clocks

steps.detail: My apps > Upgrade on the app card: verify the previously submitted info (use case, privacy policy link), upload a video recording of your app completing an action using the Pinterest API (showing the OAuth flow and a live integration), and submit. Pinterest reviews regularly and emails the decision.
steps.title: Upgrade to Standard access

tagline: OAuth behind two reviews: Trial approval before you even get credentials (with all created Pins and Boards invisible to everyone but their creator), then a Standard upgrade with a video demo before real users. Access tokens live 30 days; continuous refresh tokens run on a 60-day, refresh-or-die clock.

time.active: ~10 min of app setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code + demo recording

time.waiting: Trial review and Standard upgrade: 'a few days' guidance only, no SLA
